title: Greetings by Time of Day
explanation: Spanish has greetings that fit the time of day. The boundaries are flexible, so learn them as useful choices rather than exact clock rules.

title: Name Pattern: Me llamo...
explanation: Use me llamo plus a name to say your name. Do not change the pattern when only the name changes.

title: Origin Pattern: Soy de...
explanation: Use soy de plus a city or country to say where you are from. Keep de in the pattern.

title: Tener: tengo, tienes, tiene
explanation: Use tengo for I have, tienes for you have, and tiene for he, she, or a named person has.

title: Age with Tener
explanation: In Spanish, age is expressed with tener. At A0, learn the pattern tengo ... años.

title: Basic Question Words
explanation: Qué, cómo, dónde, and quién are written with accents in direct questions. Spanish direct questions normally begin with ¿ and end with ?.

title: Simple Word Order
explanation: A safe beginner pattern is subject plus verb plus complement. Spanish often omits yo when the verb already shows I.

title: El, La, Un, Una
explanation: At A0, learn el/la as the and un/una as a or one with familiar nouns. Do not try to memorize all gender rules yet.

title: Reading Spanish Basics
explanation: Spanish spelling is often more regular than English. Vowels are stable, h is silent, ñ is its own letter, and written accents can mark stress or meaning.

title: qu, gue, gui
explanation: Before e or i, qu represents the k sound in words like queso. In gue and gui, the u keeps g hard in words such as Miguel.
